newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank sees rates easing in 3-6 mths.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank sees rates easing in 3-6 mths.

text.p: A senior Bank of Thailand official said Thai lending rates could ease in the next three to six months as liquidity improved.

Paibool Kittisrikangwan, the chief of the central bank's analysis and money market operation division, said a likely reduction of interest rates would help boost loan growth in the second half of the year.

"The liquidity in the system is quite high, judging from the interbank rate which stands around 6.00-7.00 percent at present due to the launch of 80 billion baht in pension and provident funds," he told a seminar.
The funds are due to enter the money market gradually.
"The ample liquidity will lead the commercial banks to cut interest rates in the next three-six months and consequently boost credit expansion in the later half of the year," he said.
Paibool said if the Bank of Thailand had not increased the size of bonds issued weekly to absorb the liquidity, the interbank rate could have dropped to five percent.
The Bank of Thailand raised to 30 billion baht from 2.0 billion baht the value of its bonds for auction this Friday and to 20 billion baht from two billion baht last Friday.
Currently, the minimum lending rate charged by commercial banks stands at around 13.25 percent.
On Wednesday, Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said the government wanted current high interest rates reduced.
